以下は、留学生がスピーチのために書いた文章である。


香道

ベルナールマリー

「香道」とは、香りを楽しむ日本の伝統文化です。私は、友人が香道の体験ができる教室に誘ってくれたのをきっかけに、初めて香道のことを知りました。私は普段から香水などで香りを楽しんでいるので、香道の体験も楽しむことができました。

　香道は、「香木」と呼ばれる木の破片を熱し、その香りを楽しみます。「香木」[48]　そのような名前の木がもともと存在するわけではありません。いくつかの種類の木の中で、様々な自然条件のもとで、年月の経過によって香りを発生させるようになった木をそう呼びます。人工的に生産できないため、大変貴重なものと[49]。

　香道には600年以上の歴史がありますが、その存在はあまり知られていません。数に限りがある香木は、香道が広まり需要が増えすぎればなくなるおそれもあります。[50]、香道ではあまり多くの弟子を受け入れませんでした。香道がよく知られていないのは、そういった事情もあるそうです。

　香道では、香りをかいで、じっくりと味わうことを「香りを聞く」と言います。香りに心を傾けて聞くことを基本に、香りを聞きながら古典文学を鑑賞したり、どれがどの香木の香りかを当てて楽しんだりもします。

　繊細な香りを心の中でゆっくり味わうことを通して、私は「香りを聞く」という意味がわかったような気がしました。香水のように手軽ではありませんが、このような香りの楽しみ方も[51]。

The following is an essay written by an international student for a speech.


Kōdō

Bernard Marie

“Kōdō” is a traditional Japanese art of appreciating fragrance. I first learned about Kōdō when a friend invited me to a class where you can experience it. Because I usually enjoy scents such as perfume, I was able to enjoy the Kōdō experience as well.

 In Kōdō, fragments of wood called “incense wood” are heated and their fragrance is appreciated. “Incense wood” [48] does not refer to a tree species that originally exists under that name. Among several kinds of trees, those that, under various natural conditions over many years, come to produce fragrance are called that. Because it cannot be produced artificially, it is considered extremely precious and [49].

 Although Kōdō has a history of over 600 years, it is not very well known. Since the amount of incense wood is limited, if Kōdō spreads and demand grows too much, it may run out. [50], Kōdō did not accept very many disciples. It is said that this is one reason Kōdō is not widely known.

 In Kōdō, carefully smelling and savoring a fragrance is called “listening to the fragrance.” Based on the idea of turning one’s heart to listen to the scent, people appreciate classical literature while listening to the fragrance, and also enjoy guessing which scent belongs to which incense wood.

 By slowly savoring the delicate fragrance in my mind, I felt I came to understand the meaning of “listening to the fragrance.” It is not as easy as perfume, but this way of enjoying fragrance is also [51].

(1)

　以下は、図書館で司書(注１)が子どもたちに本を読んで聞かせることについて書かれた文章である。

　読み聞かせの時には、まず子どもたちに表紙を見せます。 そして、 ゆっくりと書名と著者や画家の名前を読み上げます。 表紙をめくると、 見返し紙が出てきて、それは無地の色紙であったり、 または本の中身とかかわる絵があったりするのですが、それもゆっくりと見せます。 ここは、 その本の中身に入る前の気持ちの準備のためのページなのです。 それから扉のページがあって、 開けるとその本の世界が広がります。

　つまり、すぐに本の中身に飛び込んでゆくのではなく、じっくりと本を見せて、 そのお話 の世界に子どもたちを案内する。 ただ子どもたちがおもしろがればいいのではなく、一人ひと りがその世界に入っていく、そうして自分で何かを感じ取る。 それが図書館でのお話し会なの です。

　その時、語り手が主役ではありません。 著者が読者に伝えたいことを、その代わりになって伝える仕事ですから、大げさな身振りや声色(注 2)よりも、 ごく (注３)自然な話し方と、そ れに伴う控えめな(注 4) 身振りで、著者の思いを伝えようとします。

　(中略)

　そこで、司書は、 読み聞かせやお話をする前に、その本を何度も読みこんで、この著者が何をいおうとするのかを考え、どこに間を入れたらよいのかを考えます。 それから練習に入ります。 読み聞かせの場合も、本文をほとんど暗記するほどに読みこむことが必要とされています。 子どもと本とを結びつけるのには、そういう配慮(注 5)と厳しい訓練が必要なのです。

(注 1）司書： 図書館の専門的な仕事をする職員
(注 2) 声色: 声の調子 
(注 3) ごく: 非常に
(注 4) 控えめな: 大げさでない 
(注 5) 配慮: ここでは、気持ち

(1)

The following passage is about librarians (Note 1) reading books aloud to children at a library.

When doing a read-aloud, first show the children the cover. Then slowly read out the title and the names of the author and illustrator. When you turn the cover, the endpapers appear—they may be plain colored paper, or they may have illustrations related to the content—and you should show those slowly as well. This page prepares the feelings before entering the content of the book. Then there is the title page, and when you open it, the world of the book unfolds.

In other words, rather than diving into the content immediately, you show the book carefully and guide the children into the story’s world. It isn’t just about letting them be amused; each child enters that world and senses something for themselves. That is what a storytime at the library is.

At that time, the storyteller is not the star. Because the job is to convey to the readers what the author wishes to communicate, in their place, we try to convey the author’s thoughts with a very (Note 3) natural way of speaking and the accompanying modest (Note 4) gestures, rather than with exaggerated gestures or voice acting (Note 2).

(Omitted)

Therefore, before doing a read-aloud or telling a story, the librarian reads the book many times, considers what the author is trying to say, and thinks about where to insert pauses. Then they practice. Even for read-alouds, it is considered necessary to read the text so thoroughly that it is almost memorized. To connect children with books requires such consideration (Note 5) and rigorous training.

(Note 1) Librarian: Staff who perform specialized work at libraries
(Note 2) Voice acting: Tone of voice
(Note 3) Very: Extremely
(Note 4) Modest: Not exaggerated
(Note 5) Consideration: Here, care and feeling

(2)

　いま、ハーバードや MIT (マサチューセッツ工科大学)、あるいは日本の京都大学でも、授業内容のインターネットでの公開を始めている。 せっかく大学に入って授業料も支払っているのに、 その内容がインターネットで見られるというのは、どういうことだろう。

　要するに、もはや (注１)そこで得られる知識や情報=コンテンツは世界共有になってしまったのだ。 かつては、東京に行かなければ得られない知識、 あるいはパリやニューヨークまで行かなければ得られない情報というものが確かにあった。 しかし、いまや(注 2)、どんな情報も知識も、インターネットで簡単に手に入れること ができる。そのことを大前提にしつつ、それでも「ここで、 共に、学ぶ」ことが重要な時代になってきたのだ。 もはや、学校の、少なくとも大学以上の高等教育機関の存在価値は、新しい知識や情報を得る場所としてではなく、共に学び、 議論し、 共同作業を行うという点だけになった。

　だとするならば、大学側も、どのような学びの共同体をそこに実現するかを、きちんと公 表していかなければならない。 どんな学生に来て欲しいのかを示すと共に、どんな教職員がそ こにいて、そこにどのような「学び」 が実現するのかを、 はつきりと示していかなければならな い。

(注１) もはや: すでに 
(注 2) いまや: いまでは

(2)

Now, Harvard, MIT, and even Kyoto University in Japan have begun to publish course content on the internet. What does it mean that, after finally getting into university and paying tuition, that content can be viewed online?

In short, the knowledge and information—the content—available there has already (Note 1) become shared worldwide. There truly used to be knowledge you could only get by going to Tokyo, or information you could only get by going as far as Paris or New York. But now (Note 2), any information or knowledge can be obtained easily on the internet. On that fundamental premise, we have entered an era in which “learning here, together” is nevertheless important. The raison d’être of schools—at least institutions of higher education above the university level—is no longer as places to obtain new knowledge or information, but solely as places to learn together, debate, and engage in collaborative work.

If that is so, universities must clearly announce what kind of learning community they will realize there. Along with indicating what kind of students they want to come, they must plainly show what faculty and staff are there, and what kind of “learning” will be realized there.

(Note 1) Already: By now
(Note 2) Now: Nowadays

(3)

　自分を見失わない(注 1)ためのコツとして、ぼくは「何でも正直に話をする」ようにしています。

　その場で波風(注 2) を立てずに、聞き心地(注 3)がいいことだけを他人に言っていたら、同じようなことを心の中で自分に対しても言うようになってしまいます。長期的に見て、「本心(注 4)を口にしない」ことの悪影響は、非常に大きいのです。自分についたウソは、気付かないうちにそれがウソか本当かもわからなくなる。自分を慰めるために言っているのか、現実がそうなのか、区別がつかなくなります。これが怖いのです。

　(中略)

　自分にウソをつかないことのメリットはもう一つあります。「記憶のコスト」が低く なるということです。

　その場の空気で調子を合わせていると、「自分がどこで何を言ったか」を記憶し ておかなければいけません。たくさんの案件(注 5)を同時進行で動かしていると、自分が どのような基準で、どう判断したかを記憶することは、すごく大変な作業になります。

　ただ正直ということを最優先していれば、忘れてしまっている案件でも、ほぼ同じ 決断に辿り着くことができます。まわりに合わせて自分にウソをついていたりすると、ま ったく逆のことを言ってしまったりして、判断がぶれる(注 6)のです。

(注 1) ～を見失う : 〜がわからなくなる。
(注 2) 波風を立てずに: ここでは、雰囲気を悪くしないで
(注 3) 聞き心地: 聞いたときの感じ
(注 4) 本心: 本当の気持ち
(注 5) 案件: ことがら
(注 6) ぶれる: ここでは、同じではなくなる

(3)

As a tip for not losing myself (Note 1), I try to “speak honestly about everything.”

If, to keep from rocking the boat (Note 2), you only say to others what is pleasant to hear (Note 3), you’ll end up saying similar things to yourself in your heart. In the long run, the negative impact of “not voicing your true feelings” (Note 4) is enormous. Lies you tell yourself can leave you unable to tell whether they’re lies or the truth before you even notice. You won’t be able to distinguish whether you’re saying something to comfort yourself or whether reality is actually that way. That’s what’s frightening.

(Omitted)

There’s another benefit to not lying to yourself: the “cost of memory” becomes lower.

If you go along with the mood of the moment, you have to remember “what you said where.” When you’re moving many matters (Note 5) forward simultaneously, remembering by what standards you judged and how is an extremely burdensome task.

If you simply prioritize honesty above all, you can arrive at almost the same decision even on matters you’ve forgotten. But if you go along with others and lie to yourself, you may end up saying the complete opposite, and your judgments will waver (Note 6).

(Note 1) To lose sight of ~: To no longer understand ~
(Note 2) Without stirring up waves: Here, without making the atmosphere unpleasant
(Note 3) Pleasant to hear: How it feels when heard
(Note 4) True feelings: One’s real feelings
(Note 5) Matters: Items, cases
(Note 6) Waver: Here, to be inconsistent

(4)

　以下は、いい写真を撮りたいと思っている人に向けて書かれた文章である。

　ポートフォリオ(注 1)を作ることには大きく二つの意味がある。まず自分のため、そしてもう一つは他者に見せる(プレゼンテーションする)ためだ。写真を撮り続けるうちに、だんだん自分が何をしようとしているのかが見えてくる。被写体(注2) について漠然とした(注3)認識(注4)しか持てなかったのが、はっきりと焦点が絞られてきて、このやり方でいいのだという自信が芽生えてくる。そうなったらポートフォリオを作ってみるといい。

　よく「形にしてみないとわからない」というが、これは本当だと思う。作品をまとめる ことで、 自信が確信に変わることがよくあるからだ。逆にポートフォリオにしてみると、自分の写真の弱点もよく見えてくる。撮影中には見過ごしていた( 注 5)ことが、後で冷静に見直すとくっきりと浮かび上がってくるのだ。欠けていたものを修整する(注6)ことで、作品をさらによくすることができるだろう。

　他人に見せるというのも大事なことだ。写真をどこかで発表したいとか、写真家と して仕事をしたいという人は当然だが、そこまで考えていなくてもポートフォリオを人に 見せるのはとても有意義だと思う。自分の作品がどれくらいのレベルにあるのか、どの 程度のインパクトを持っているのか客観的に判断するきっかけになるからだ。

　(中略)

　作品は他者にきちんと届いて初めて価値を持つ。自己完結した(注 7)小さな世界が、 受け手とのキャッチボールでより大きなものになっていく。その第一歩としてポートフォリ オを誰かに見せてみよう。

(注 1) ポートフォリオ: ここでは、自分が撮った写真をまとめたもの
(注 2)被写体: 写真に撮られる対象
(注 3)漠然とした: ぼんやりとした
(注 4)認識: ここでは、捉え方
(注 5) 見過ごしている: ここでは、気づいていない
(注 6)修整する: ここでは、補う
(注 7) 自己完結した: ここでは、自分だけで出来上がった

(4)

The following passage is for people who want to take better photographs.

Creating a portfolio (Note 1) has two major purposes: first, for yourself, and second, to show to others (to present). As you keep taking photos, you gradually come to see what you’re trying to do. Where you once had only a vague (Note 3) understanding (Note 4) of your subject (Note 2), the focus becomes clear and you gain confidence that this approach is right. When that happens, try making a portfolio.

It’s often said, “You won’t know until you make it into a form,” and I believe that’s true. By assembling your works, confidence often turns into conviction. Conversely, when you make a portfolio, the weaknesses in your photos also become clear. Things you overlooked (Note 5) during shooting stand out sharply when you calmly review them later. By correcting (Note 6) what was missing, you can likely make your work even better.

Showing your work to others is also important. Of course this applies to those who want to present their photos somewhere or work as photographers, but even if you haven’t thought that far, I think showing your portfolio to people is very meaningful. It gives you a chance to judge objectively what level your work is at and how much impact it has.

(Omitted)

A work only has value once it properly reaches others. A small, self-contained (Note 7) world grows larger through a back-and-forth with the audience. As a first step, try showing your portfolio to someone.

(Note 1) Portfolio: Here, a collection of your own photographs
(Note 2) Subject: What is photographed
(Note 3) Vague: Fuzzy, indistinct
(Note 4) Understanding: Here, way of grasping
(Note 5) Overlooked: Here, not noticed
(Note 6) Correct: Here, to supplement what was lacking
(Note 7) Self-contained: Here, completed by oneself alone

p_question-4583.ja:
A


　会社で働いていれば、部下に仕事を教える立場になることがあるだろう。そんなとき、 私はできるだけ社内用語や専門用語を使わずに、誰が聞いても分かる言葉で説明す るようにしている。教える側と教えられる側の知識や経験には大きな差があるからだ。

　いずれ覚えなければならないからと思って最初から難しい言葉を使って説明すると、仕事自体が難しいという印象を与え、部下が仕事を理解しようという意欲を失ってしまう。大切なのは、部下の能力に応じた教え方をすることではないだろうか。部下にとって分かりやすい言葉で仕事をしっかり理解させ、やる気を引き出すことは、上司の大事な役目だ。

A

If you work at a company, there will be times when you’re in a position to teach subordinates their work. At such times, I try as much as possible to avoid using in-house jargon and technical terms, and instead explain in words anyone can understand. That’s because there is a large gap in knowledge and experience between the teacher and the learner.

If you think “they’ll have to learn it eventually” and explain using difficult terms from the start, you give the impression that the work itself is difficult and rob subordinates of the motivation to try to understand it. What’s important is to teach in a way that suits their abilities. 大きな感動をあたえてくれた場所には、またいきたくなる。できれば、その場所にいつまでも居つづけたい。そう思うのは、人の自然な感情だ。

　宇宙飛行士の毛利衛さんにとっては、「宇宙」が、その場所だった。

　スペース・シャトルでの初めての宇宙飛行から帰還してからは、しばらくは講演活動やマネージメントの仕事をしていたらしいが、そんな生活が、物足りなくてしょうがない。ひとつの夢を果たし終えて、自分の人生まで終わってしまったように思えてくる。「もう一度、宇宙へいきたい」という気持ちがわいてくるのも自然な感情だろう。

　張り詰めた緊張感のある生活を、もう一度送りたい。宇宙から地球を見たときの、その感動を、もう一度味わいたい・・・・・・。

　二度目の宇宙飛行への挑戦（注１） を決心したとき、毛利さんはすでに四十八歳になっていた。すでに若くはない人間にとってはつらい訓練でもあったが、どうにか（注 2）乗り越えて、ふたたび宇宙へ旅立った。

毛利さんばかりではないように思う。プロ野球選手は、いつまでもグラウンドに立ちつづけたいと思うだろうし、サラリーマンは定年になっても、職場から離れがたく思うものだろう。その場所を去らなければならない「とき」がやってくる。毛利さんも、じつはそのことは、二度目の訓練を受けているときから薄々（注3）感じていた。体力も反射神経（注4）も、もう若い人にはかなわない（注5）。

　宇宙飛行は、希望すればだれでもいけるというものではない。スペース・シャトルには「定員」があるし、選ばれなければ宇宙へはいけない。

「三度目」はないかもしれない。後ろ髪を引かれる（注 6）ような寂しさはあるが、しかし、 いまの毛利さんには、「なにがなんでも（注 7）、もう一度」という強いこだわりはないのだ という。

　それは、新しい「生きがい」を見つけることができたからだそうだ。自分には経験があ る。知識もある。いつまでも若い人と競うのではなく、自分が得てきたものを若い人たち に伝えてゆく「喜び」もあるのではないか。

　自分の夢を追い求める人生から、次の世代の人たちの夢の応援する人生へ。たしかに、そのような発想の転換ができれば、新しい「生きがい」を見つけるのも早そうだ。

　次の世代に夢をつなげていくのは、「老兵」の重要な仕事なのである。

（注４）反射神経：ここでは、反応する速さ

We want to go back to places that moved us deeply. If possible, we want to stay there forever. Feeling that way is only natural.

For astronaut Mamoru Mohri, that place was “space.”

After returning from his first spaceflight on the Space Shuttle, he apparently spent some time giving lectures and doing management work, but such a life felt unsatisfying to him. Having fulfilled one dream, it felt as if his life itself had ended. It’s only natural that the feeling “I want to go to space once more” welled up.

He wanted once again to live a life taut with tension. He wanted to savor once more the emotion he felt when he looked at Earth from space...

When he decided to take on the challenge (Note 1) of a second spaceflight, Mohri was already 48. The training was hard for someone no longer young, but he somehow (Note 2) got through it and set off for space again.

He is probably not alone in this. Professional baseball players likely want to keep standing on the field forever, and office workers, even at retirement, likely find it hard to leave the workplace. The “time” comes when one must leave that place. Mohri, in fact, had sensed this vaguely (Note 3) ever since he was undergoing training for the second time. Neither his stamina nor his reflexes (Note 4) could match (Note 5) those of the young anymore.

Spaceflight is not something anyone can do just because they want to. The Space Shuttle has a set “capacity,” and unless you are selected, you cannot go to space.

There might not be a “third time.” There is a lingering sadness, as if one’s hair were being pulled from behind (Note 6), but Mohri now says he no longer has a strong insistence of “no matter what (Note 7), once more.”

That’s because he has found a new “purpose in life.” He has experience. He has knowledge. Rather than competing with young people forever, isn’t there also joy in passing on what he has gained to the younger generation?

From a life of pursuing his own dreams to a life of supporting the dreams of the next generation. Indeed, if one can make such a shift in thinking, one might find a new “purpose in life” quickly.

Passing dreams on to the next generation is an important task of the “old soldier.”

(Note 1) Challenge: A challenge
(Note 2) Somehow: Somehow, with effort
(Note 3) Vaguely: Faintly, in a general way
(Note 4) Reflexes: Here, speed of response
(Note 5) Can’t match: Can’t beat
(Note 6) As if one’s hair were being pulled from behind: Here, hard to give up
(Note 7) No matter what: At all costs

**Word Translation**  
早期（そうき） — early stage, initial stage

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
Due to advances in medicine, diseases can now be detected at an early stage.

**Explanation**  
The word **早期** is used to describe an early or initial phase of a process or condition, particularly in contexts like disease detection. "早期の段階" (early stage) is a common expression in Japanese, often used in medical or procedural contexts to indicate timeliness or the beginning phase.

① 夏休みの__早期__は旅行をして、その後は試験勉強をする予定だ。  
→ During the early part of summer vacation, I plan to travel, and then study for exams.  
🔶 Unnatural Usage  
"早期" is generally not used to talk about vacation periods. More common would be "始め" (beginning) or "初め" (initial part) of a period.

② 明日の飛行機は__早期__の便だから、朝5時に家を出なければならない。  
→ Tomorrow’s flight is an early one, so I have to leave home at 5 AM.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"早期" is not appropriate for describing the timing of flights. "早い便" or "朝一の便" (early flight) would be natural.

③ 一人暮らしの__早期__は、料理などの失敗も多くて苦労した。  
→ In the early stage of living alone, I struggled with many cooking failures.  
🔶 Unnatural Usage  
While "early period" fits the context, "早期" is rarely used for personal life stages. "初期" (beginning period) or "最初" (initial) would be more appropriate.

**Usage Note**  
"早期" is typically used in formal or technical contexts, such as medicine, strategy, or procedure, where the emphasis is on identifying or acting during an early phase. It does not usually apply to casual descriptions of time or individual experiences.

④ あの人は偉大な馬を何頭も飼っている。  
→ That person owns many great horses.  
❌ Incorrect Usage

**Explanation**

"妨げる" is typically used in contexts where the action directly causes a delay, obstacle, or interference with a particular process or event, such as "進行" (progress) or "活動" (activity). It is not used in contexts where the intention is prevention or securing.

Answer (★ Position)
Answer 1: こと

Correct Order
4 → 3 → 1 → 2
📌 すれ違っても → 目を合わせる → こと → すら

Chunk-by-Chunk Breakdown
④ すれ違っても — “even when (we) pass each other”; sets the condition
③ 目を合わせる — “to make eye contact”; verb phrase base
① こと — nominaliser; turns the verb phrase into a noun phrase
② すら — “even”; emphasizes the extremity with a negative

Reconstructed Sentence
隣のクラスの友達とけんかしてしまい、学校の廊下で**すれ違っても、目を合わせることすら**なくなってしまった。
→ “I ended up fighting with my friend from the next class, and now even when we pass each other in the hallway, we don’t even make eye contact anymore.”

Why This Order Works
“目を合わせる” needs nominalising by **こと** so that **すら** can attach to the noun phrase (**〜ことすら〜ない**), giving the emphasis “not even do X.” The conditional **すれ違っても** naturally precedes the main clause.

Passage:  
(1)  
If you can stop expecting things from others from the beginning, neither anger nor irritation will arise, and you can spend your days with a calm mind. The passage emphasizes the idea that by stopping to expect things from others, you can maintain a peaceful and calm mindset. The passage highlights the concept of letting go of "期待" (きたい), which means "expectations," to achieve a calm state ("穏やかな気持ち" - おだやかなきもち). Understanding how relinquishing expectations leads to a calm demeanor is crucial in interpreting the author's intention in this context.

**Question Translation**  
What is being communicated in this email?

**Explanation**  
The passage is a request from an employee to the general affairs department, asking to open the meeting room during lunchtime so more people can use it to take breaks or have lunch, alleviating the overcrowding issue in the current break room. The correct answer (2) accurately captures the core request: to use the meeting room as an additional break room during lunchtime to accommodate more people.

questions.stem: 生物について、 筆者の考えに合うのはどれか。
opts: ある環境で競争に負けても、自分に合った別の環境で生き残れる。
多様な環境の中で自らを変化させなければ、競争に勝てない。
競争に負けた生物は、場所を変えずにそこで生きられるように変化する。
競争に勝たなければ、すべての環境条件で生き残れない。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: ある環境で競争に負けても、自分に合った別の環境で生き残れる。 It means "Even if you are defeated in the competition in one environment, you can survive in another environment that suits you."

**Question Translation**  
Regarding living organisms, which option matches the author's opinion?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the importance of diverse environments in the biological world. It emphasizes that no organism can be the winner in every environmental condition, but competition allows organisms to find environments that suit them. The passage suggests that different conditions can change winners into losers and vice versa, highlighting that the diversity of environments is crucial for organisms to find suitable habitats. This aligns with Answer 1, which states that even if an organism loses in one environment, it can survive in another that fits it better.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: "多様な環境の中で自らを変化させなければ、競争に勝てない" means "If you do not change yourself in a diverse environment, you cannot win in the competition." This does not fit the passage, as it emphasizes adaptation within a single environment rather than finding different suitable environments.
- Answer 3: "競争に負けた生物は、場所を変えずにそこで生きられるように変化する" means "Organisms that lose in competition change to survive without moving to another place." This suggests adaptation in the same environment, contradicting the passage's idea of finding a new suitable environment.
- Answer 4: "競争に勝たなければ、すべての環境条件で生き残れない" means "If you don’t win in the competition, you cannot survive in all environmental conditions." This implies that winning is necessary for survival in all conditions, which the passage disputes by stressing that no organism can win in every condition.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The key vocabulary includes "生物社会" (せいぶつしゃかい, biological society) and "多様な環境" (たようなかんきょう, diverse environments), highlighting how organisms interact within ecosystems. The phrase "自分に適した環境" (じぶんにてきしたかんきょう, environment suitable for oneself) is crucial to understanding that organisms find niches rather than adapt to any and all conditions.

questions.stem: このメールで店員が問い合わせていることは何か。
opts: 電源の状態が悪くなる可能性があるが、画面の修理をするかどうか。
追加で料金と時間がかかるが、電源の修理もするかどうか。

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: 追加で料金と時間がかかるが、電源の修理もするかどうか。 This translates to "It will cost an additional fee and take more time, but do you want to have the power supply repaired as well?"

**Question Translation**  
What is the store clerk inquiring about in this email?

**Explanation**  
The email is a communication from a computer store clerk indicating that while a laptop's screen is being repaired, an additional issue has been found with the power supply parts. The email states the connection might worsen, and it is recommended that the customer considers replacing the part. The repair will incur an additional charge of 20,000 yen and delay the return to June 10th. However, if the customer chooses not to repair the power supply, the screen repair will be completed, and the product will be returned as scheduled on June 5th. The clerk is inquiring whether the customer wishes to go forward with the additional repair, thus confirming Answer 2 as the correct answer.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 1**: 電源の状態が悪くなる可能性があるが、画面の修理をするかどうか。 ("There is a possibility the power supply may worsen, but whether to repair the screen.") This is incorrect because the primary concern of the inquiry is not whether to proceed with the screen repair, which is already in progress, but about the additional power supply repair.
  
- **Answer 3**: 追加で料金がかかるが、電源の修理を6月5日までに終えるかどうか。 ("It will cost an additional fee, but whether to complete the power supply repair by June 5th.") This choice is incorrect because it suggests completing the power repair by June 5th, which contrasts with the email's statement that repairs would extend the return date beyond June 5th.

- **Answer 4**: 6月5日に画面と電源の修理は完了するが、いつ受け取りに来るか。 ("The screen and power supply repair will be completed on June 5th, but when to pick it up.") This is incorrect because it misrepresents the repair timeline, wrongly stating that both repairs would be completed by June 5th, which contradicts the email's details.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- "追加で料金" (ついかでりょうきん) means "additional fee". 
- "電源" (でんげん) refers to "power supply."
- Understanding nuances in conditional sentences and polite inquiries is crucial to deducing the clerk is asking for the customer's decision regarding additional repairs.

questions.stem: 生きている世代に対して、 筆者が言いたいことは何か。
opts: 今生きている世代があげている反府や怒りの声を聞くべきだ。
今生きている世代にも声があげられない人がいることを認めるべきだ。
未来の世代が生きていくために、必要な資源を見つけるべきだ。
声をあげられない未来の世代のことを考え、行動を改めるべきだ。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4: 声をあげられない未来の世代のことを考え、行動を改めるべきだ。 This means "We should consider the future generations who cannot raise their voices and change our actions."

**Question Translation**  
What does the author mean to say about the living generation?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the inability of future generations to voice opposition or anger about the actions taken by the current generation that damage the environment and deplete resources, which are essential for their survival. The author highlights this concern, calling into question the fairness of these actions. Thus, the author is urging the current generation to consider the impact of their actions on future generations who cannot speak for themselves and to change their behavior accordingly. This idea is best captured in Answer 4, which suggests being mindful of future generations and modifying actions.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 1:** 今生きている世代があげている反府や怒りの声を聞くべきだ。 "We should listen to the voices of opposition and anger raised by the living generation." This choice is incorrect because the passage is more concerned with the inability of future generations to raise their voices, not emphasizing the voices of the current generation.
  
- **Answer 2:** 今生きている世代にも声があげられない人がいることを認めるべきだ。 "We should acknowledge that there are people in the current generation who cannot raise their voices." The focus is misplaced here, as the text centers on future generations who cannot speak out, rather than individuals in the current generation.
  
- **Answer 3:** 未来の世代が生きていくために、必要な資源を見つけるべきだ。 "We should find necessary resources for the future generations to live." The passage already implies that current generations are consuming these resources; it doesn't suggest finding new ones but urges to stop depleting the existing ones. The main argument is about altering current harmful actions, not finding new resources.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- **抗議（こうぎ）:** In this context, emphasized as opposition or anger.
- **絶対条件（ぜったいじょうけん）:** Critical condition, necessary condition.
  
The usage of "それをいいことに," meaning to take advantage of a situation, highlights the author's point on how current generations exploit the silence of future ones. Understanding this phrase is crucial to grasping the author's critique.

本の中身に飛び込めるように、表紙と絵の多いページを見せる。

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 本の世界に入れるように、時間をかけて表紙から見せていく is correct. It means "Show the cover slowly to allow them to enter the world of the book."

**Question Translation**  
What kind of preparation does the storyteller make for the children before reading aloud?

**Explanation**  
The passage describes the methodical approach taken by the librarian to prepare children before reading to them. The storyteller doesn't rush into the content but takes the time to show the book's cover and introduce the title, author, and possibly related illustrations. This approach is to guide the children into the world of the story gradually. The correct answer reflects this process by emphasizing the slow and deliberate presentation of the book cover as a means to help the children enter the book's world.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 2**: 本の中身に飛び込めるように、表紙と絵の多いページを見せる. This suggests showing the cover and pages with many illustrations to allow the children to dive into the story. However, the passage emphasizes a slow reveal instead and is not focused on pages with many illustrations.
- **Answer 3**: 関心を高めるために、表紙を見せながら多くの情報を伝える. This implies providing a lot of information to raise interest while showing the cover, but the passage stresses a natural and simple presentation without overwhelming details.
- **Answer 4**: 自分で何かを感じ取れるように、表紙から自由にめくらせる. It suggests letting children freely turn the pages from the cover, whereas the passage indicates a guided introduction rather than allowing children to explore on their own.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- **読み聞かせ (よみきかせ)**: Refers to the practice of reading aloud to others, often used in the context of storytelling to children.
- The concept of pacing and gradual introduction (じっくりと) is crucial in understanding the storyteller's method, highlighting the importance of preparing the mind for immersion in the story.

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4 is correct. It means "With the spread of the internet, the value of institutions as a place to acquire knowledge or information has been lost."

**Question Translation**  
Which of the following aligns with the author's view about current universities?

**Explanation**  
In the passage, the author discusses how the availability of university lecture content on the internet has changed the role of higher education institutions. The author states that knowledge and information have become globally shared resources due to the internet. As a result, the traditional role of universities as places to acquire new knowledge and information is being replaced by their role as centers for collaborative learning and discussion. This aligns with Answer 4, which emphasizes that universities are no longer valued primarily as places to obtain knowledge or information because it can now be accessed online.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: This option states that paying tuition has lost its meaning due to public lecture content, which is a misunderstanding. The passage emphasizes that universities have shifted their focus to collaborative learning, not diminishing the value of tuition fees.
- Answer 2: This misinterpretation suggests that universities are unnecessary due to the ability to learn from anywhere, but the passage advocates for the importance of learning communities and collaboration, highlighting the continued relevance of choosing a university.
- Answer 3: While internet development has made education more accessible, the passage specifically focuses on the change in the role of institutions, not leveling educational standards worldwide.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- "もはや" (もはや) - An adverb meaning "already," indicating that a change has already occurred.
- "いまや" (いまや) - An adverb meaning "by now" or "now," suggesting the current state of affairs in contrast to the past.
- "共同" (きょうどう) - Refers to "collaborative" or "joint," a key concept in the passage about the future direction of universities focusing on collaborative learning over traditional roles.

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: 学びの共同体として、何ができるかを具体的に示す必要がある。 It means "It is necessary to specifically demonstrate what can be done as a learning community."

**Question Translation**  
Regarding universities, what does the author want to convey?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the shifting role of universities in a world where knowledge and information are increasingly accessible online. The author highlights the need for universities to focus on the importance of "learning together," which means engaging in discussions and collaborative work. The text stresses that higher education institutions should clearly demonstrate what type of learning community they can establish. Thus, Answer 3 aligns perfectly with the author’s argument, as it emphasizes the necessity for universities to explicitly show what they can achieve as a learning community.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 学生が求めている学びの共同体を実現するべきだ。 This means "A learning community that students are seeking should be realized." This focuses too much on student desires rather than the necessity for the university to present its collaborative capabilities explicitly.
- Answer 2: ほかでは得られない情報や知識を提供する必要がある。 This means "It's necessary to provide information and knowledge that cannot be obtained elsewhere." This statement contradicts the passage, which states that universities are no longer primarily places to access unique information and knowledge.
- Answer 4: どのような学びの共同体を作るかを、学生自身にも考えさせるべきだ。 This means "Students themselves should also be made to think about what kind of learning community to create." While involving students in the process might be beneficial, the passage emphasizes the university's responsibility to clearly define and communicate its role as a learning community, not to offload this task onto students.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- The phrase もはや (もはや, already) indicates a completed change, suggesting that past norms are no longer applicable, reflecting the shift in how universities contribute to education.
- The term 学びの共同体 (まなびのきょうどうたい, learning community) refers to an environment in which students and faculty engage collaboratively beyond mere consumption of content. Recognizing such expressions can aid in grasping the author's intention.

questions.stem: 筆者によると、自分の本当の気持ちを言わないでいるとどうなるか。
opts: 自分が本当だと思っていることがわからなくなる。
自分の本当の気持ちを常に隠すようになる。
他人と自分の気持ちの区別がつきにくくなる。
他人との関係がうまくいかなくなる。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 自分が本当だと思っていることがわからなくなる。 It means "You won't be able to know what you truly believe is true."

**Question Translation**  
According to the author, what happens if you don’t express your true feelings?

**Explanation**  
The correct answer is the best fit because the passage states that failing to express one’s true feelings can distort one's understanding of what is true or false, as the person becomes unable to distinguish between comforting lies and reality. The author mentions that not expressing your true feelings has significant negative impacts because it confuses one's sense of truth and leads to uncertainty about whether one's internal statements are for self-comfort or reflect reality.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: 自分の本当の気持ちを常に隠すようになる (You will always hide your true feelings)—This is incorrect because the passage discusses the consequences of not expressing one's true feelings, emphasizing the loss of understanding truth rather than developing a habit of hiding one's feelings entirely.
- Answer 3: 他人と自分の気持ちの区別がつきにくくなる (It becomes difficult to distinguish between others' and your own feelings)—The passage focuses on confusion between truth and self-deceptive thoughts rather than confusion between self and others' feelings.
- Answer 4: 他人との関係がうまくいかなくなる (Relationships with others will not go well)—Although this could be a consequence, the passage does not explicitly discuss direct impacts on interpersonal relationships but rather on personal confusion.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- 本心 (ほんしん): Meaning "true feelings," is emphasized to highlight the importance of honesty with oneself.
- The concept of “自分についたウソ” (lies to oneself) underscores the potential for personal integrity and self-understanding to deteriorate when one avoids expressing true feelings. Recognizing such nuanced vocabulary can enhance comprehension.

questions.stem: 「記憶のコスト」が低くなるとはどういうことか。
opts: 判断の基準を覚えていなくても、その場の空気に合わせて判断ができる。
判断の基準だけ覚えていれば、正しい決断ができる。
自分が言ったことを覚えていなくても、同じ決断ができる。
正直に話したことだけを思い出せば、同じ決断ができる。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: 自分が言ったことを覚えていなくても、同じ決断ができる。 It means, "Even if you don't remember what you said, you can arrive at the same decision."

**Question Translation**  
What does it mean when the "cost of memory" becomes lower?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the concept of "記憶のコスト" (memory cost) in the context of always being honest. When you don't lie, you don't need to remember what you said on different occasions. By being honest, you reduce the complexity and burden of keeping track of past statements, thus arriving at consistent decisions even if you forget previous specifics. This aligns with the idea that by prioritizing honesty, one can naturally reach similar conclusions regardless of past forgotten details, as opposed to remembering every single word said under varying circumstances.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 判断の基準を覚えていなくても、その場の空気に合わせて判断ができる。 "Even if you don't remember the criteria of your decisions, you can adjust your judgment to fit the atmosphere at that moment." This suggests decision-making based on current context rather than consistency linked to honesty, which is not what the passage emphasizes.
  
- Answer 2: 判断の基準だけ覚えていれば、正しい決断ができる。 "If you only remember your criteria for decision-making, you can make correct decisions." This option implies accuracy based on remembered criteria, but the passage emphasizes decision consistency through honesty, not remembrance of criteria.

- Answer 4: 正直に話したことだけを思い出せば、同じ決断ができる。 "If you only remember what you have talked about honestly, you can make the same decision." While it partially captures the essence, the focus here is on memory dependence rather than the reduced need for it with honesty.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- 「記憶のコスト」 literally translates to "cost of memory," indicating the mental effort required to recall past actions or statements.
- The verb "ぶれる" in this context means to deviate or waver, highlighting inconsistency when one lies. Recognizing how context modifies the usage of certain words can help with comprehension in similar passages.

questions.stem: 筆者によると、いつポートフォリオを作ってみるのがいいか。
opts: 自分の写真を他人に見てもらって、自信を持ちたいと思ったとき。
自分の撮りたい写真が明確になって、自信がついてきたとき。
対象をさまざまな捉え方で撮れるようになったとき。
いい写真が撮れて、人に見せたいと思ったとき。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: 自分の撮りたい写真が明確になって、自信がついてきたとき。 It means "when your desired photography subject becomes clear, and confidence begins to emerge."

**Question Translation**  
According to the author, when is the best time to try creating a portfolio?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the process of making a portfolio and suggests making one when your understanding of what you want to achieve becomes clear and you start gaining confidence in your photography style. This is described in the passage as "だんだん自分が何をしようとしているのかが見えてくる" and "このやり方でいいのだという自信が芽生えてくる," which aligns with Answer 2.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 1:** "自分の写真を他人に見てもらって、自信を持ちたいと思ったとき" means "when you want others to see your photos and gain confidence." The passage suggests that confidence in your photography should already be building before you create a portfolio.
- **Answer 3:** "対象をさまざまな捉え方で撮れるようになったとき" means "when you can photograph subjects with various perspectives." The passage emphasizes clarity and confidence in your intentions rather than the variety in perspective when deciding to create a portfolio.
- **Answer 4:** "いい写真が撮れて、人に見せたいと思ったとき" means "when you take good photos and want to show them to others." This option focuses on the desire to show others, while the passage focuses on clarity of purpose and internal confidence before making a portfolio.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- **焦点が絞られてきて (しょうてんがしぼられてきて):** This phrase means "to focus clearly," and it indicates the clarity of one's photographic purpose.
- **自信が芽生えてくる (じしんがめばえてくる):** This means "confidence begins to sprout" or "confidence starts to develop," which is crucial in the context for when to start a portfolio. Recognizing these phrases helps identify the correct context and timing for creating a portfolio.

questions.stem: 筆者によると、ポートフォリオを他人に見せるといいのはなぜか。
opts: 自分が写真家になれるレベルかどうかがわかるから。
作品を他人が正しく理解したかどうかがわかるから。
作品の欠点がわかり、新しい撮り方ができるから。
作品に対する他人の評価を知ることができるから。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4: 作品に対する他人の評価を知ることができるから。 It means "Because you can learn how others evaluate your work."

**Question Translation**  
According to the author, why is it beneficial to show your portfolio to others?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the significance of creating a portfolio both for oneself and for presentation to others. It emphasizes that showing your portfolio to others provides an opportunity to objectively assess the level and impact of your work through external evaluations. This aligns with the author's view that understanding how your work is perceived by others adds value and significance to your work, suggesting that outside opinions can transform a self-contained world into a larger, more impactful creation. This is why Answer 4 is the best fit—it directly addresses the benefit of gaining external perspective and evaluation, as mentioned in the passage.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 1:** 自分が写真家になれるレベルかどうかがわかるから。 ("Because you can determine whether you are at the level to become a photographer.") 
  - The passage does not suggest that showing your portfolio helps establish whether you reach a professional level as a photographer. While it provides insight into your work's impact, it doesn't specifically determine career readiness.
  
- **Answer 2:** 作品を他人が正しく理解したかどうかがわかるから。 ("Because you can see whether others correctly understand your work.")
  - The passage mentions evaluating the level and impact of your work, not whether others understand it correctly. The focus is more on gaining an objective assessment rather than testing for accurate understanding.
  
- **Answer 3:** 作品の欠点がわかり、新しい撮り方ができるから。 ("Because you can find out the flaws in your work and take new kinds of photos.")
  - The passage indicates that compiling a portfolio helps highlight weaknesses, but this option is more aligned with personal reflection and improvement rather than gaining insights from others. The emphasis on "new kinds of photos" is also unrelated to the main benefit of showing the portfolio to others.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- **客観的に判断する** (きゃっかんてきに はんだんする): "To objectively judge." This phrase is crucial in understanding why outside evaluation is stressed, reinforcing the idea that getting feedback from others provides a more impartial look at your work.
- **評価** (ひょうか): "Evaluation." Recognizing this term helps in understanding that the focus is on gathering others' assessments of your work.

questions.stem: A と B は、それぞれ仕事をどのように教えていると述べているか。
opts: も B も、難しい言葉を使わずに簡単な言葉で教えていると述べている。
A も B も、部下が担当する仕事と一緒に、関連する仕事も教えていると述べている。
A は部下がすぐに覚えられる仕事を先に教えていると述べ、B は仕事の内容を絞って教えていると述べている。
A は部下が理解しやすい言葉を使って教えていると述べ、B は部下が担当する仕事に限定して教えていると述べている。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4 is correct. It means A explains in words that are easy for subordinates to understand, while B limits the teaching to the specific tasks the subordinates are responsible for.

**Question Translation**  
How are A and B explaining their teaching methods?

**Explanation**  
The correct answer identifies the different approaches to teaching methods as described by A and B. A mentions using easy-to-understand language to ensure the subordinates grasp the job tasks without being overwhelmed by complex terminology. B, on the other hand, focuses on limiting the teaching scope to the subordinates’ immediate responsibilities. This helps them learn at an appropriate pace and ensures they fully grasp their tasks without an overload of information.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: This option incorrectly states that both A and B emphasize using simple words. While A does mention this approach, B focuses more on limiting the teaching to specific tasks rather than the simplicity of language.
- Answer 2: This option is inaccurate because neither A nor B talks about teaching additional related tasks. A is about ensuring understanding with simple words, and B is about limiting the teaching to immediate responsibilities.
- Answer 3: This option inaccurately interprets A’s method. A is more focused on simplifying language, not necessarily teaching tasks that can be quickly memorized. B’s approach of limiting the scope is accurately mentioned, but A’s process is not described correctly.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- **社内用語（しゃないようご）**: This refers to company-specific terminology, which A aims to avoid when teaching to make the instructions clearer to subordinates.
- **一気に教え込もうとする**: This phrase from B’s passage means "trying to teach many things at once," which B argues against in favor of a more focused approach to teaching tasks.
- **部下（ぶか）**: A term for subordinates or junior employees who are being instructed on their jobs. Understanding the relationships and hierarchy in a company setting is crucial for interpreting the passage correctly.

questions.stem: 仕事を教える際に重要なこととして、A と B が共通して述べていることは何か。
opts: 部下のやる気を引き出すこと。
部下の長所を見つけて伸ばすこと。
部下の能力に合わせて指導すること。
部下とのよい関係を維持すること。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: 部下の能力に合わせて指導すること (ぶかののうりょくにあわせてしどうすること) is correct. It means "to instruct according to the abilities of subordinates."

**Question Translation**  
What do A and B both mention as important when it comes to teaching work?

**Explanation**  
Both passages from A and B mention the necessity of tailoring the instruction to the subordinate's abilities and experience. In A, it specifies avoiding complex jargon and adapting explanations to the subordinate's comprehension to motivate them to learn. B emphasizes understanding the subordinate's knowledge and experience and adjusting the content and speed of teaching accordingly. Both passages therefore highlight instructing based on the subordinate's capability as a key point.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 部下のやる気を引き出すこと ("to draw out subordinates' motivation") is mentioned in A but not in B. While increasing motivation is important, B does not explicitly state this as a main point.
  
- Answer 2: 部下の長所を見つけて伸ばすこと ("to find and develop the subordinates' strengths") is not a shared point in the passages. While B discusses focusing on what subordinates can do, A does not emphasize identifying and expanding strengths.

- Answer 4: 部下とのよい関係を維持すること ("to maintain a good relationship with subordinates") is not addressed in either passage as a main topic. Both texts focus more on the teaching approach rather than personal relationships.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- 部下 (ぶか) means "subordinate" and is commonly used in workplace contexts to refer to those who report to a manager or leader.
- 指導する (しどうする) means "to instruct" or "to guide," emphasizing adapting methods to fit individual needs in this context. Understanding nuances in how to instruct others is vital, especially when highlighting individualized approaches in workplace settings.

questions.stem: 筆者によると、初めての宇宙飛行から帰ってきたあと、毛利さんはどのように感じ ていたか。
opts: 宇宙飛行のような大きな夢を持って生活を送りたい。
宇宙でやり残したもうひとつの夢を果たしたい。
経験したことを生かすために、また宇宙へいきたい。
緊張感や感動を得るために、また宇宙へいきたい。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**
Answer 4 is correct. It means "He wanted to go to space again to regain the sense of tension and that moving feeling."

**Question Translation**
"According to the author, how did Mr. Mōri feel after returning from his first spaceflight?"

**Explanation**
The passage says: after his first mission, everyday work felt unsatisfying, and he naturally felt, "I want to go to space once more." Specifically, he wanted to **live again with taut tension** and **taste again the emotion** he felt seeing Earth from space. This matches option 4 exactly.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**
1. 「[宇宙]飛行のような大きな夢を持って生活を送りたい。」
→ "I want to live my life carrying a big dream like spaceflight."  
He wasn’t talking about carrying a new big dream in daily life; he longed to **re-experience** space for its tension and emotion. ❌

2. 「[宇宙]でやり残したもうひとつの夢を果たしたい。」
→ "I want to fulfill another unfinished dream in space."  
No “unfinished second dream” is mentioned. He simply wanted to go again. ❌

3. 「経験したことを生かすために、また[宇宙]へいきたい。」
→ "I want to go to space again to make use of my experience."  
His motive given is **not** to utilize experience, but to feel the tension and emotion again. ❌

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**
張り詰めた緊張感＝"high-strung/taut sense of tension"; 感動を味わう＝"to savor/experience deep emotion." These nouns clearly signal the emotional motivation in option 4.

questions.stem: 筆者が言いたいことは何か。
opts: 自分の夢を追い求めたあとは、若い人の夢を応援することが大切だ。
夢はひとつだけではないことを若い人に伝えて、応援するべきだ。
若い人の夢を応援しながら、自分の夢も追い求めつづけたほうがいい。
若い人の夢を応援するには、さまざまな経験や知識が必要だ。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 自分の夢を追い求めたあとは、若い人の夢を応援することが大切だ。  
This means: After pursuing one's own dreams, it is important to support the dreams of young people.

**Question Translation**  
What is the author's main message?

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses 毛利 (Mori), an astronaut who, after fulfilling his own dream of space travel, finds a new purpose in supporting the next generation. It emphasizes the transition from pursuing personal dreams to helping others achieve theirs. The text underscores finding new "ikigai" (meaning or purpose in life) by assisting young people and passing on experiences and knowledge. Answer 1 encapsulates this thematic message, highlighting the importance of supporting others' dreams once one's own have been pursued.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: "夢はひとつだけではないことを若い人に伝えて、応援するべきだ。"  
  This suggests a focus on telling young people that dreams can be multiple. While the passage discusses supporting young people's dreams, it doesn't emphasize the multiplicity of dreams. The key theme is supporting the next generation after fulfilling personal dreams, not necessarily the nature or number of dreams.

- Answer 3: "若い人の夢を応援しながら、自分の夢も追い求めつづけたほうがいい。"  
  This implies continuing to pursue personal dreams while supporting young people’s dreams. However, the passage conveys Mori’s shift in focus from pursuing his own dreams to exclusively supporting younger generations. The suggestion of pursuing both simultaneously is not consistent with the thematic conclusion of the text.

- Answer 4: "若い人の夢を応援するには、さまざまな経験や知識が必要だ。"  
  While the passage mentions that Mori has experience and knowledge, the primary theme is not about the necessity of these for supporting others' dreams. Instead, it’s about the fulfillment and importance of transitioning to support the dreams of others after pursuing one’s own.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- "生きがい" (いきがい): A Japanese term meaning "reason for living" or "purpose in life". Understanding this concept helps to comprehend the shift in Mori's purpose from his own dreams to encouraging the dreams of the younger generation.
- "後ろ髪を引かれる": An idiomatic expression meaning to feel reluctance or sadness when leaving something behind, indicating Mori’s bittersweet feelings about moving on from his personal dreams.

questions.stem:
アニカさんは友達と３人で一緒に、ハイキングに行くことにした。ハイキングのコースは、 「お勧めコース」から選びたいと思っている。アニカさんは３人の希望をメモに書いた。３人の希 望に最も合うコースはどれか。

アニカさんのメモ

テイエ……登山鉄道に乗りたい。
サナ……「合計時間」が、2時間までのものがいい。
アニカ……スタートとゴールは違う場所にしたい。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**
Answer 2 is correct. It means "The 'Enjoy the Flowers' course."

**Question Translation**
"Annika decided to go hiking with two friends (three people total). They want to pick a route from the 'Recommended Courses.' Annika wrote down everyone’s wishes. Which course best matches all three?"

**Explanation**
Requirements:  
• テイエ—ride the **mountain railway (登山鉄道)**.  
• サナ—**total time ≤ 2 hours**.  
• アニカ—**different start and goal** locations.

「花を楽しむコース」 uses the mountain railway (北口→山頂), has **1.5 hours** total, and starts at **北口** but ends at **南口**—different places. Therefore, it satisfies all three conditions.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**
1. 「らくらくコース。」  
→ "Easy course."  
Time 1 hour and includes the railway, but **starts and ends at 北口** (same place). ❌

3. 「半周コース。」  
→ "Half-loop course."  
Time 1.5 hours and different start/end (南口→北口), but **no mountain railway** (all on foot). ❌

4. 「一周コース。」  
→ "Full-loop course."  
Includes the railway and different start/end, but **total time is 3 hours**, exceeding 2 hours. ❌

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**
合計時間＝"total time" (includes breaks); 登山鉄道＝"mountain railway/cog railway."

questions.stem:
ダンさんは、１０月に会社の同僚１５人とガイドツアーを利用したいと思っている。申し込
みにあたり気をつけなければならないこととして、合っているのはどれか。
opts: 申し込みはツアーを希望する日の３日前の午後６時までに電話する必要がある。
ガイド料金はどの「お勧めコース」を選ぶかによって変わる。
申し込みはまとめてできるが、当日は複数のグループに分かれなければならない。
出発時間は、午前８時３０分から午前１１時までの間で指定する必要がある。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**
Answer 3 is correct. It means "You can apply together, but on the day you must split into multiple groups."

**Question Translation**
"Mr. Dan wants to use a guided tour in **October** with 15 coworkers. In applying, which point he must be careful about is correct?"

**Explanation**
The guide states: **capacity per group is 10 people**; for **11 or more**, participants will be **split into multiple groups on the day**. With 15 people, they can submit one application but must divide into groups then—exactly option 3.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**
1. 「申し込みはツアーを希望する日の３日前の午後６時までに電話する必要がある。」  
→ "You must call to apply by 6 p.m. three days before the tour date."  
Wrong deadline. Applications are accepted **until 6 p.m. ten days before**; "three days" is for **cancellations**. ❌

2. 「ガイド料金はどの『お勧めコース』を選ぶかによって変わる。」  
→ "The guide fee varies depending on the recommended course chosen."  
Incorrect; the guide fee is **500 yen per person for any course**. ❌

4. 「出発時間は、午前８時３０分から午前１１時までの間で指定する必要がある。」  
→ "You must specify a departure time between 8:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m."  
In **October (10月)**, opening time is **9:00 a.m.** (Oct–Mar). Thus departures must be **9:00–11:00**, not from 8:30. ❌

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**
定員＝"capacity, limit"; ～までの間で指定＝"specify within the time window." Recognizing seasonal time differences (4–9月 vs 10–3月) is key for option 4.

questions.script_html: 博物館で職員3人が小学生向けの科学教室の企画について話しています 次の子ども科学教室空気中で音が伝わる仕組みっていうテーマだったよねなかなかいい企画だけど今のままだと時間をオーバーしそうだから内容を削りたいんだ 今の案では前半で仕組みを説明して後半で身近なもので楽器を作るっていう工作をする構成になってますよね ストローを使った笛と空き缶を使った太鼓内容を削るなら 工作を2つじゃなくて一つにしましょうか何度も試作したんですよ 工作は両方残しましょうよじゃあ前半の説明を短くするのはどうですか説明のところもう十分短くしてありますよね そうだねーそこはこれ以上カットするとただの工作教室になっちゃうから企画と合わないよねー工作は2つ紹介してどちらかやりたい方を子供が選んで作れるようにしたらどうですか なるほどねーどっちにするか迷って時間がかからないように進行の仕方を検討する必要がありそうだけど 他にはストローとか空き缶とか工作の材料をこちらで事前に切っておいて準備の時間を短縮するという手もありますがそれでそんなに時間が変わるでしょうか そうだねーそれに準備するところから子供たちに体験してもらいたいから そうすると子供に選んでもらうさっきの案にしよう 3人は内容をどう変更することにしましたか1紹介する工作を1つにする 2前半の説明を短くする3作らせる工作を1つにする 4工作の材料を切っておくラジオを聞いて女の学生と男の学生が話しています 来週から1週間山川市で桜映画祭が行われます 干渉の仕方が少し珍しい映画を4つご紹介しますまずはアニメ映画の白い雲 映画を見ながら歌ったり手を叩いたりしてもいいことになっているので賑やかに楽しめます それからミステリー映画の緑の列車こちらはオーケストラが映像に合わせて生で音楽を演奏します 恋愛映画美しい一日の会場は今回の映画祭で唯一の屋外の会場です山川公園に臨時でスクリーンが設置されます 今はいい季節だから気持ちがいいでしょうね最後にミュージカル映画旅の空 会場のレストランで食事を楽しみながら観賞できます今言ってた映画祭2人用のチケットが2枚あるんだけど一緒に見に行かない 2つ見られるから一つずつ選ぼうえっいいの僕前に映画の音楽に合わせてみんなで歌ってもいいっていう映画 見に行ったことがあるんだけど一体感があって楽しかったよへー 日本では静かに見ましょうっていう映画館の方が多いけどねうんあの雰囲気をまた味わいたいなぁいいね1つはそれにしよ 私は美味しい食事を楽しみながらっていうのも魅力的だけど 開放感がある外で見てみたいなじゃあそうしよう質問1 男の学生はどの映画を選びましたか質問に 女の学生はどの映画を選びましたか
